intro: This is Fildamı Cistern, in İstanbul province, built in the 5th century AD. The open cistern at Bakırköy held the water of the imperial palace at Hebdomon, and its walls, 127 metres by 76, still stand to full height.
history: The open cistern at Bakırköy was built in the fifth century AD to hold the water of the imperial palace at Hebdomon. Look at its walls: 127 metres by 76, and still standing to full height. Under the Ottomans it was drained and worked as a market garden, and its Turkish name dates from those years.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the cistern walls and their buttresses. Find the inlet channel, and look for the remains of Hebdomon.
facts: Did you know? Hebdomon was where Byzantine emperors were crowned before the army, and this cistern supplied that ceremonial ground with water. The walls of the open cistern, 127 metres by 76, still stand to full height.
outro: This brings our tour of Fildamı Cistern to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Enjoy your visit.
